title: I don't know where I put it
goal: On campus, tell Sēf you've lost your student card and don't know what to do or who to ask
tip: To say 'I don't know where / what / when…', put ma adri in front of the question and keep its normal word order: wēn il-maktab? → ma adri wēn il-maktab 'I don't know where the office is'. shu asawwi? → ma adri shu asawwi 'I don't know what to do'.
grammar: indirect questions: ma adri + wēn, shu, mita, lēsh, minu + a normal clause
dialogue: A
شفيك يا ريّال؟ شو صار؟
shfīk yā rayyāl? shu ṣār?
What's up, man? What happened?
B
بطاقة الجامعة ضاعت. ما أدري وين حطيتها
biṭāgat il-jāmʿa ẓāʿat. ma adri wēn ḥaṭṭēt-ha
My student card's gone. I don't know where I put it.
A
شفت في الشنطة؟
shift fi sh-shanṭa?
Did you look in your bag?
B
هيه، ما لقيتها. ما أدري شو أسوي
hē, ma ligēt-ha. ma adri shu asawwi
I did, but I couldn't find it. I don't know what to do.
A
روح المكتب اللي قدام المكتبة، هم يعرفون
rūḥ il-maktab illi jiddām il-maktaba, hum yaʿarfūn
Go to the office in front of the library, they'll know.
B
زين. بس ما أدري منو أكلم هناك
zēn. bas ma adri minu akallim hnāk
OK. But I don't know who to talk to there.
A
ما أدري متى يسكرون. إذا تبي، نروح الحين
ma adri mita ysakkrūn. idha tabi, nrūḥ il-ḥīn
I don't know when they close. If you want, let's go now.
B
يلا. ما أدري ليش أغراضي دوم تضيع!
yalla. ma adri lēsh aghrāẓi dōm tẓīʿ!
Let's go. I don't know why my stuff always goes missing!
items: ma adri wēn ḥaṭṭēt-ha = I don't know where I put it; fast speech: madri wēn
I don't know what to do
Kuwait: ma adri shinu asawwi (ما أدري شنو أسوي)
ma adri mita ysakkrūn = I don't know when they close
I don't know who to talk to
akallim = I talk to, I call (someone)
before a noun, biṭāga becomes biṭāgat
they close, they shut (a shop, an office)
it closes: ysakkir (يسكر); they open: yiftaḥūn (يفتحون)
your things: aghrāẓak (to a man), aghrāẓich (to a woman)

title: Do you know where the meeting room is?
goal: At the office, ask Maryam if she knows where the meeting is, who's coming and why the manager picked you
tip: To ask a colleague, start with tadri…? 'do you know…?' and add the question as it is: tadri wēn il-mudīr? 'do you know where the manager is?'. To a woman: tadrīn…? or taʿarfīn…?: tadrīn minu yāy? On its own, tadri shu? means 'you know what?'.
grammar: indirect questions: tadri / tadrīn / taʿarfīn + wēn, shu, minu, mita
dialogue: B
مريم، تدرين وين غرفة الاجتماعات اليديدة؟
Maryam, tadrīn wēn ghurfat il-ijtimāʿāt il-yidīda?
Maryam, do you know where the new meeting room is?
A
هيه، في الطابق الثالث. ليش؟
hē, fi ṭ-ṭābig ith-thālith. lēsh?
Yes, on the third floor. Why?
B
عندنا ضيوف الساعة عشر. تدرين منو ياي؟
ʿindana ẓyūf is-sāʿa ʿashr. tadrīn minu yāy?
We've got visitors at ten. Do you know who's coming?
A
ما أدري والله. بس تدري شو؟ المدير يبيك تسوي العرض
ma adri wallāh. bas tadri shu? il-mudīr yabīk tsawwi l-ʿarẓ
No idea. But you know what? The manager wants you to give the presentation.
B
أنا؟ تدرين ليش اختارني أنا؟
ana? tadrīn lēsh ikhtārni ana?
Me? Do you know why he picked me?
A
يقول إنك تتكلم زين
ygūl innak titkallam zēn
He says you speak well.
B
الله يستر! تعرفين متى يخلص الاجتماع؟
allāh yistur! taʿarfīn mita yikhlaṣ il-ijtimāʿ?
Heaven help me! Do you know when the meeting finishes?
A
قبل الغدا إن شاء الله. لا تخاف، بتسويه زين
gabil il-ghada in shāʼ allāh. la tkhāf, bitsawwīh zēn
Before lunch, hopefully. Don't worry, you'll do it well.
items: do you know where…? (to a woman)
to a man: tadri wēn…? (تدري وين؟)
to a woman: tadrīn shu?; before a clause it asks 'do you know what…?': tadri shu ṣār?
do you know who…? (to a woman)
to a man: tadri minu…? (تدري منو؟)
do you know when…? (to a woman)
to a man: taʿarf mita…? (تعرف متى؟); taʿarf and tadri both mean 'you know'
he wants you to do (to a man)
to a woman: yabīch tsawwīn (يبيج تسوين)
heaven help me, let's hope it goes all right (lit. may God protect)
said before something worrying, half joking or serious

title: Could you tell me where it is?
goal: Ask at a mall information desk where to buy a phone charger and when the mall closes
tip: gūl-li 'tell me' + a question asks for information: gūl-li shu tabi 'tell me what you want'. To a stranger, soften it with mumkin: mumkin tgūl-li wēn il-maṭāʿim? 'could you tell me where the restaurants are?'. To a woman: mumkin tgūlīn-li…?
grammar: indirect questions after gūl-li 'tell me': mumkin tgūl-li wēn…?, gūl-li shu…
dialogue: B
السلام عليكم. ممكن تقول لي وين محلات التلفونات؟
as-salāmu ʿalaykum. mumkin tgūl-li wēn maḥallāt it-tilifōnāt?
Hello. Could you tell me where the phone shops are?
A
وعليكم السلام. في وايد. قول لي شو تبي بالضبط
wa ʿalaykum is-salām. fī wāyid. gūl-li shu tabi biẓ-ẓabṭ
Hello. There are lots. Tell me what exactly you want.
B
شاحن حق تلفوني. كان في محل هني، ما أدري شو اسمه
shāḥin ḥagg tilifōni. kān fī maḥall hni, ma adri shu ismah
A charger for my phone. There was a shop here, I don't know what it's called.
A
حق أي تلفون؟
ḥagg ay tilifōn?
For which phone?
B
حق هذا. ووين أقرب محل، لو سمحت؟
ḥagg hādha. w wēn agrab maḥall, law samaḥt?
For this one. And where's the nearest shop, please?
A
في الطابق الأول، يم المطاعم
fi ṭ-ṭābig il-awwal, yamm il-maṭāʿim
On the first floor, next to the restaurants.
B
مشكور. وممكن تقول لي متى يسكر المول؟
mashkūr. w mumkin tgūl-li mita ysakkir il-mōl?
Thanks. And could you tell me when the mall closes?
A
العفو. نص الليل، بس المحلات تسكر قبل
il-ʿafu. nuṣṣ il-lēl, bas il-maḥallāt tsakkir gabil
You're welcome. At midnight, but the shops close earlier.
items: could you tell me…? (to a man)
to a woman: mumkin tgūlīn-li…? (ممكن تقولين لي؟)
to a woman: gūlī-li shu (قولي لي شو), you'll see written قوليلي شو; to a man you'll also see قولي شو
I don't know what it's called, I don't know his name
a feminine noun or a woman: ma adri shu ismha (ما أدري شو اسمها)
after a vowel: fi ṭ-ṭābig il-awwal
next to the restaurants, by the restaurants
when does it open?: mita yiftaḥ? (متى يفتح؟)
there are lots, there are plenty
culture: Even at a counter, start with as-salāmu ʿalaykum before your question, and wait for the reply: going straight to the question can sound abrupt. With shop and mall staff, mumkin…? and law samaḥt are polite enough; long formal phrases sound stiff in Gulf speech.

title: Ask him if there's a table outside
goal: Phone a restaurant worker to book for your mates, ask whether there's a table outside, and say you'll get back to them
tip: idha also means 'whether': ma adri idha fī makān 'I don't know if there's room'. Use it after asʼal 'ask', shūf 'see, check' and ma adri: isʼalah idha yigdar 'ask him if he can'. The question after idha keeps its normal word order.
grammar: idha 'whether, if' after asʼal, shūf and ma adri: isʼalah idha…
dialogue: B
السلام عليكم. أبي أسأل إذا عندكم طاولة باكر في الليل
as-salāmu ʿalaykum. abi asʼal idha ʿindakum ṭāwla bāchir fi l-lēl
Hello. I'd like to ask if you have a table tomorrow night.
A
وعليكم السلام. حق كم واحد؟
wa ʿalaykum is-salām. ḥagg cham wāḥid?
Hello. For how many?
B
حق خمسة. وشوف إذا في طاولة برا، لو سمحت
ḥagg khamsa. w shūf idha fī ṭāwla barra, law samaḥt
For five. And see if there's a table outside, please.
A
برا كله محجوز. بس المدير يمكن يقدر يسوي شي
barra killah maḥjūz. bas il-mudīr yimkin yigdar ysawwi shay
Outside is all booked. But the manager might be able to do something.
B
زين، اسأله إذا يقدر. نحب نقعد برا
zēn, isʼalah idha yigdar. nḥibb nigʿid barra
OK, ask him if he can. We like sitting outside.
A
سألته. يقول إن في طاولة الساعة تسع
saʼaltah. ygūl inn fī ṭāwla s-sāʿa tisʿ
I asked him. He says there's a table at nine.
B
ما أدري إذا ربعي يقدرون الساعة تسع. بسألهم وبرد عليك
ma adri idha rabʿi yigdarūn is-sāʿa tisʿ. basʼalhum w barudd ʿalēk
I don't know if my mates can make it at nine. I'll ask them and get back to you.
A
ما عليه. بس لا تتأخر، باكر زحمة
ma ʿalēh. bas la titʼakhkhar, bāchir zaḥma
No problem. But don't leave it late, tomorrow's busy.
items: I'd like to ask if, I'm calling to ask whether
a polite way to start a call to a shop, a clinic or an office
ask him whether, ask him if (to a man)
to a woman: isʼalīh idha (اسأليه إذا)
I don't know if, I don't know whether
see if, check whether (to a man)
to a woman: shūfi idha (شوفي إذا)
it's all booked, it's fully booked
a feminine noun: iṭ-ṭāwla maḥjūza (الطاولة محجوزة)
I'll get back to you, I'll let you know (to a man)
to a woman: barudd ʿalēch (برد عليج)

title: Checkpoint 3.2: Fahad's flight is late
goal: Checkpoint: from Dubai airport, phone Fahad to find out why his flight is late and what to do
tip: The 'I don't know where / if' pattern works with every person: ma nadri 'we don't know', ma tadri 'she doesn't know', ma yadri 'he doesn't know'. To a group, tadri becomes tadrūn: tadrūn shu? 'you know what, guys?'. Fahad says shinu for shu: ma adri shinu ṣāyir, tadrūn shinu?
grammar: checkpoint 3.2: recycle s3u013–s3u027 (conditionals, reported speech, indirect questions)
dialogue: B
هلا فهد! وينك؟ نحن في المطار
hala Fahad! wēnak? niḥin fi l-maṭār
Hi Fahad! Where are you? We're at the airport.
A
هلا والله. للحين في الكويت! يقولون إن الطيارة متأخرة
hala wallāh. lil-ḥīn fi l-Kwēt! ygūlūn inn iṭ-ṭayyāra mitʼakhkhra
Hi. I'm still in Kuwait! They say the flight's delayed.
B
صج؟ ما ندري شي! تدري ليش؟
ṣij? ma nadri shay! tadri lēsh?
Really? We had no idea! Do you know why?
A
لا والله، ما أدري شنو صاير. حتى الموظفة ما تدري
la wallāh, ma adri shinu ṣāyir. ḥatta l-muwaẓẓafa ma tadri
No, I've no idea what's going on. Even the woman at the desk doesn't know.
B
ما عليه. سيف يقول بنترياك حتى لو تأخرت وايد
ma ʿalēh. Sēf ygūl binitrayyāk ḥatta lō taʼakhkhart wāyid
Never mind. Sēf says we'll wait for you even if you're really late.
A
تدرون شنو؟ روحوا البيت. إذا وصلت، باخذ تاكسي
tadrūn shinu? rūḥu l-bēt. idha wiṣalt, bākhidh tāksi
You know what, guys? Go home. When I land, I'll take a taxi.
B
لا، بنترياك. بس اسألها إذا في طيارة ثانية
la, binitrayyāk. bas isʼalha idha fī ṭayyāra thānya
No, we'll wait for you. But ask her if there's another flight.
A
زين، بسألها. وإذا عرفت شي، بطرش لكم
zēn, basʼalha. w idha ʿiraft shay, baṭarrish-lkum
OK, I'll ask her. And if I find out anything, I'll message you.
items: ma nadri shay = we've no idea; Kuwait: the same (iḥna ma nadri)
he doesn't know: ma yadri (ما يدري); to a man it also means 'you don't know'
do you know why? (to a man)
to a woman: tadrīn lēsh? (تدرين ليش؟)
to one man: tadri shinu?; to one woman: tadrīn shinu?; UAE: tadrūn shu? (تدرون شو؟)
ask her whether, ask her if (to a man)
to a woman: isʼalīha idha (اسأليها إذا)
UAE: ma adri shu (ما أدري شو)

title: Who fixes the printer?
goal: Find the office technician, tell him what's wrong with the printer, and encourage him while he works
tip: Many everyday verbs double their middle letter: ṣallaḥ 'he fixed', yṣalliḥ 'he fixes'. You know some already: sawwa, ṭarrash, khallaṣ. They take the usual endings: aṣalliḥ 'I fix', tṣalliḥ 'you fix', yṣallḥūn 'they fix'. With 'it': aṣalliḥha 'I fix it (f.)', baṣalliḥha 'I'll fix it (f.)'.
grammar: Form II verbs (doubled middle letter): yṣalliḥ 'he fixes', aṣalliḥha 'I fix it (f.)'
dialogue: B
لو سمحت، منو اللي يصلح الطابعة؟
law samaḥt, minu illi yṣalliḥ iṭ-ṭābʿa?
Excuse me, who fixes the printer?
A
أنا. شو فيها؟
ana. shu fīha?
Me. What's wrong with it?
B
ما تطبع من الصبح. ما أدري شو صار لها
ma tiṭbaʿ min iṣ-ṣubḥ. ma adri shu ṣār-lha
It hasn't printed since this morning. I don't know what's happened to it.
A
بسيطة. خلني أشوفها وأصلحها الحين
basīṭa. khallni ashūfha w aṣalliḥha l-ḥīn
No problem. Let me look at it and I'll fix it now.
B
الله يقويك! تبي شي؟
allāh ygawwīk! tabi shay?
More power to you! Do you need anything?
A
الله يعافيك. خلاص، اشتغلت! بس لا تحطون فيها ورق وايد
allāh yʿāfīk. khalāṣ, ishtaghalat! bas la tḥuṭṭūn fīha warag wāyid
Thank you. There, it's working! But don't (any of you) put too much paper in it.
B
ما شاء الله! ما قصرت
mā shāʼ allāh! mā gaṣṣart
Brilliant! Thanks so much.
A
ما سوينا شي. إذا خربت مرة ثانية، قول لي
mā sawwēna shay. idha khirbat marra thānya, gūl-li
It was nothing. If it breaks down again, tell me.
items: I fix: aṣalliḥ (أصلح); he fixed: ṣallaḥ (صلح); don't confuse with ma yiṣlaḥ 'it won't do', spelled the same
(let me) fix it (f.), I fix it
I'll fix it: baṣalliḥha (بصلحها); a masculine thing: aṣallḥah (أصلحه)
(to someone working) God give you strength (to a man)
to a woman: allāh ygawwīch (الله يقويج); a common reply: allāh yʿāfīk
what's happened to it (f.)?, what's happened to her?
a masculine thing or a man: shu ṣār-lah? (شو صار له؟)
a masculine thing: idha khirib (إذا خرب)
it's working now, it worked (a feminine thing)
a masculine thing: ishtaghal (اشتغل); not ishtaghalt 'I worked', written the same
culture: allāh ygawwīk is what you say to someone in the middle of a job: a technician, a cleaner, friends carrying furniture. yaʿṭīk il-ʿāfya, which you already know, works in the same places. Both are warm and everyday, not formal, and you can say them to anyone working, whatever their job.

title: I changed the meeting time
goal: Talk with Maryam at the office about the meeting she moved and the slides you changed
tip: Form II past works like any past verb: ghayyart 'I changed; you (m.) changed', ghayyarti 'you (f.) changed', ghayyar 'he changed', ghayyarna 'we changed'. Add -ah for 'it': ghayyartah 'I changed it'. To a woman, -ti becomes -tī before it: ghayyartīh 'you (f.) changed it'.
grammar: Form II past: ghayyart 'I changed', ghayyartīh 'you (f.) changed it', rajjiʿha 'put it back'
dialogue: A
شفت الإيميل؟ غيرت موعد الاجتماع
shift il-īmēl? ghayyart mawʿid il-ijtimāʿ
Did you see the email? I've changed the meeting time.
B
لا، للحين ما شفته. ليش غيرتيه؟
la, lil-ḥīn ma shiftah. lēsh ghayyartīh?
No, I haven't seen it yet. Why did you change it?
A
المدير مسافر باكر. غيرته، صار يوم الخميس
il-mudīr msāfir bāchir. ghayyartah, ṣār yōm il-khamīs
The manager's flying out tomorrow. I moved it, it's on Thursday now.
B
زين. وأنا غيرت العرض شوي. تبين تشوفينه؟
zēn. w ana ghayyart il-ʿarẓ shwayy. tabīn tshūfīnah?
OK. And I've changed the presentation a bit. Do you want to see it?
A
هيه أكيد… بس ليش غيرت الألوان؟
hē akīd… bas lēsh ghayyart il-alwān?
Yes, sure… but why did you change the colours?
B
غيرت رأيي. الألوان القديمة ما كانت حلوة
ghayyart raʼyi. il-alwān il-gadīma ma kānat ḥilwa
I changed my mind. The old colours weren't nice.
A
لا والله، كانت أحلى! رجعها مثل قبل
la wallāh, kānat aḥla! rajjiʿha mithil gabil
No way, they were nicer! Put them back like before.
B
إن شاء الله. برجعها الحين
in shāʼ allāh. barajjiʿha l-ḥīn
All right. I'll change them back now.
items: I changed; you changed (to a man)
to a woman: ghayyarti (غيرتي); we changed: ghayyarna (غيرنا)
I changed it (m.), I moved it (a time, a plan); you changed it (to a man)
a feminine thing: ghayyart-ha (غيرتها); to a woman (you changed it): ghayyartīh (غيرتيه)
why did you change it? (to a woman)
to a man: lēsh ghayyartah? (ليش غيرته؟)
do you want to see it (m.)? (to a woman)
to a man: tabi tshūfah? (تبي تشوفه؟)
put it (f.) back, change them back (to a man)
to a woman: rajjʿīha (رجعيها); a masculine thing: rajjʿah (رجعه)
I'll put it (f.) back, I'll change them back
not barjaʿ 'I'll go back', which is written the same before the ending
like before, the way it was

title: Take me to the repair shop
goal: Ask Sēf to take you to get your laptop fixed and to drop you home afterwards
tip: wadda 'take (someone somewhere)' and waṣṣal 'give a lift, drop off' are Form II verbs. Add the person: waddni 'take me', bawaddīk 'I'll take you', waṣṣilni l-bēt 'drop me home'. The place follows with no word for 'to': waddni l-mōl 'take me to the mall'.
grammar: Form II with object endings: waddni 'take me', bawaddīk 'I'll take you', bawaṣṣlak 'I'll drop you'
dialogue: B
سيف، انت فاضي العصر؟ ودني محل التصليح
Sēf, inta fāẓi l-ʿaṣir? waddni maḥall it-taṣlīḥ
Sēf, are you free this afternoon? Take me to the repair shop.
A
أكيد. شو خربان؟
akīd. shu kharbān?
Sure. What's broken?
B
اللابتوب. ما يشتغل من أمس
il-lābtōb. ma yishtaghil min ams
The laptop. It hasn't worked since yesterday.
A
زين، بوديك بعد المحاضرة. أمس وديت أخوي نفس المحل
zēn, bawaddīk baʿd il-muḥāẓra. ams waddēt akhūy nafs il-maḥall
OK, I'll take you after the lecture. Yesterday I took my brother to the same shop.
B
صج؟ وزين شغلهم؟
ṣij? w zēn shughulhum?
Really? And are they any good?
A
وايد زين، وسريعين بعد
wāyid zēn, w sarīʿīn baʿad
Really good, and quick too.
B
زين. وبعدين وصلني البيت إذا تقدر
zēn. w baʿdēn waṣṣilni l-bēt idha tigdar
Great. And then drop me home, if you can.
A
لا تشيل هم. بوصلك وبنتعشى بعد
la tshīl ham. bawaṣṣlak w binitʿashsha baʿad
Don't worry about it. I'll drop you, and we'll have dinner too.
items: to a woman: waddīni (وديني); waddni l-bēt = take me home
I took (someone somewhere); you took (to a man)
drop me home, give me a lift home (to a man)
to a woman: waṣṣlīni l-bēt (وصليني البيت); not wiṣalni 'it reached me', written the same
I'll give you a lift, I'll drop you (to a man)
it doesn't work, it's not working (a masculine thing)
a feminine thing: ma tishtaghil (ما تشتغل)
don't worry about it (to a man)
to a woman: la tshīlīn ham (لا تشيلين هم); to a group: la tshīlūn ham (لا تشيلون هم)
one man: sarīʿ (سريع); a woman: sarīʿa (سريعة)

title: I've looked everywhere!
goal: At Sēf's house after the guys have gone, look for your lost phone with Sēf's help
tip: dawwar ʿala means 'look for': dawwart ʿalēh 'I looked for it (m.)'. ẓayyaʿ means 'lose (something)': ẓayyaʿtah 'I lost it'. Both are Form II: past dawwart, ẓayyaʿt; present adawwir, aẓayyiʿ; to a man, dawwir ʿalēh! 'look for it!'.
grammar: Form II: dawwart 'I looked for', ẓayyaʿtah 'I lost it', dawwir ʿalēh 'look for it!'
dialogue: B
سيف، شفت تلفوني؟ شكلي ضيعته
Sēf, shift tilifōni? shakli ẓayyaʿtah
Sēf, have you seen my phone? I think I've lost it.
A
لا والله. دورت في السيارة؟
la wallāh. dawwart fi s-sayyāra?
No. Did you look in the car?
B
هيه، دورت في كل مكان. ما لقيته
hē, dawwart fi kill makān. ma ligētah
Yes, I've looked everywhere. I can't find it.
A
خلني أدق عليه
khallni adigg ʿalēh
Let me ring it.
B
يمكن على الصامت. ما أدري وين حطيته
yimkin ʿala ṣ-ṣāmit. ma adri wēn ḥaṭṭētah
It might be on silent. I don't know where I put it.
A
اسمع! أسمعه… تحت المخدة في المجلس!
ismaʿ! asmaʿah… taḥt il-mkhadda fi l-majlis!
Listen! I can hear it… under the cushion in the majlis!
B
الحمد لله! دورت عليه نص ساعة
il-ḥamdu lillāh! dawwart ʿalēh nuṣṣ sāʿa
Thank God! I looked for it for half an hour.
A
المرة الياية دور عليه زين قبل لا تخاف
il-marra l-yāya dawwir ʿalēh zēn gabil la tkhāf
Next time, look for it properly before you panic.
items: I looked (for); you looked (to a man)
I looked for it (m.), I looked for him
a feminine thing: dawwart ʿalēha (دورت عليها)
look for it (m.), look for him (to a man)
to a woman: dawwri ʿalēh (دوري عليه)
I lost it (m.); you lost it (to a man)
a feminine thing: ẓayyaʿt-ha (ضيعتها); to a woman (you lost it): ẓayyaʿtīh (ضيعتيه); I lost: ẓayyaʿt (ضيعت)
did you look in the car? (to a man)
to a woman: dawwarti fi s-sayyāra?; dawwar fi = look in (a place), dawwar ʿala = look for (a thing)
under the cushion, under the pillow
I can hear it (m.), I can hear him
I can hear it (f.), her: asmaʿha (أسمعها); not ismaʿah 'listen to him!' (اسمعه)

title: Done, sir
goal: Report to the manager on what you've finished and what's still left, and answer him respectfully
tip: khallaṣ 'finish (something)' is Form II: khallaṣt 'I finished', khallaṣtah 'I finished it', khallaṣna 'we finished', bakhallṣah 'I'll finish it'. Without the double letter, yikhlaṣ means 'it ends, it's over': mita yikhlaṣ il-ijtimāʿ?
grammar: Form II past and future with 'it': khallaṣtah 'I finished it', bakhallṣah 'I'll finish it'
dialogue: A
صباح الخير. خلصت التقرير؟
ṣabāḥ il-khēr. khallaṣt it-taqrīr?
Morning. Have you finished the report?
B
صباح النور طال عمرك. هيه، خلصته أمس
ṣabāḥ in-nūr ṭāl ʿumrak. hē, khallaṣtah ams
Good morning, sir. Yes, I finished it yesterday.
A
زين. وطرشته لمريم؟
zēn. w ṭarrashtah l-Maryam?
Good. And did you send it to Maryam?
B
لا، للحين ما طرشته. بطرشه الحين
la, lil-ḥīn ma ṭarrashtah. baṭarrshah il-ḥīn
No, I haven't sent it yet. I'll send it now.
A
وجهزت الجدول حق اجتماع باكر؟
w jahhazt il-jadwal ḥagg ijtimāʿ bāchir?
And have you got the agenda ready for tomorrow's meeting?
B
أنا ومريم خلصنا نصه. بخلصه قبل الغدا
ana w Maryam khallaṣna nuṣṣah. bakhallṣah gabil il-ghada
Maryam and I have done half of it. I'll finish it before lunch.
A
الله يقويك. وإذا تبي شي، قول لي
allāh ygawwīk. w idha tabi shay, gūl-li
Keep it up. And if you need anything, tell me.
B
الله يعافيك. أبشر طال عمرك
allāh yʿāfīk. abshir ṭāl ʿumrak
Thank you. Will do, sir.
items: I finished; you finished (to a man)
to a woman: khallaṣti (خلصتي); khallaṣt? = have you finished?; not khilṣat 'it (f.) ended', written the same
I finished it (m.); you finished it (to a man)
a feminine thing: khallaṣt-ha (خلصتها); to a woman (you finished it): khallaṣtīh (خلصتيه)
I got (it) ready, I prepared; you prepared (to a man)
the schedule, the timetable; (for a meeting) the agenda
if you need anything (to a man)
to a woman: idha tabīn shay (إذا تبين شي)
culture: In a Gulf office, rank shows in how people talk. With a senior manager, add ṭāl ʿumrak, answer a request with abshir or abshir ṭāl ʿumrak, and keep yā rayyāl, khēba and English slang for colleagues your own age. If he encourages you with allāh ygawwīk, answer allāh yʿāfīk.

title: Is the room ready, everyone?
goal: Check with Maryam and the team that the meeting room is ready for the visitors, and thank them
tip: Form II verbs take the group endings like any past verb: rattabna 'we set out', jahhazna 'we got ready'; jahhaztu? 'have you (all) got it ready?'. Some come from English: chayyak 'check' gives chayyakt 'I checked', tchayyik 'you check'.
grammar: Form II with 'we' and 'you all': rattabna 'we set out', jahhaztu 'you (all) got ready', chayyakt 'I checked'
dialogue: B
صباح الخير يا جماعة. جهزتوا غرفة الاجتماعات؟
ṣabāḥ il-khēr yā jamāʿa. jahhaztu ghurfat il-ijtimāʿāt?
Morning, everyone. Have you got the meeting room ready?
A
صباح النور. هيه، رتبنا الكراسي وحطينا الماي
ṣabāḥ in-nūr. hē, rattabna l-karāsi w ḥaṭṭēna l-māy
Morning. Yes, we've set out the chairs and put the water out.
B
يعطيكم العافية! والشاشة؟ منو شيك عليها؟
yaʿṭīkum il-ʿāfya! w ish-shāsha? minu chayyak ʿalēha?
Thanks for all your work! And the screen? Who checked it?
A
الله يعافيك. أنا شيكت، بس ما تشتغل
allāh yʿāfīk. ana chayyakt, bas ma tishtaghil
Thank you. I checked, but it's not working.
B
يمكن السلك. خلني أشوف… خلاص، اشتغلت!
yimkin is-silk. khallni ashūf… khalāṣ, ishtaghalat!
Maybe it's the cable. Let me see… there, it's working!
A
ما شاء الله عليك! بس للحين ما سوينا القهوة
mā shāʼ allāh ʿalēk! bas lil-ḥīn ma sawwēna l-gahwa
Well done you! But we still haven't made the coffee.
B
لا تشيلون هم، أنا بسويها. الضيوف يايين الساعة عشر
la tshīlūn ham, ana basawwīha. iẓ-ẓyūf yāyīn is-sāʿa ʿashr
Don't worry, I'll make it. The visitors are coming at ten.
A
زين. وأنا برتب الأوراق على الطاولة
zēn. w ana barattib il-awrāg ʿala ṭ-ṭāwla
Good. And I'll lay out the papers on the table.
items: you (all) got (it) ready; have you got it ready? (to a group)
to one man: jahhazt; to one woman: jahhazti; you'll see written جهزتو
we tidied, we set out, we arranged
thanks for all your work (to a group)
to one man: yaʿṭīk il-ʿāfya; reply: allāh yʿāfīk
I checked; you checked (to a man)
to a woman: chayyakti (شيكتي); from English 'check'; chayyik ʿala = check (something)
the cable, the lead, the wire
I'll make it (f.), I'll do it (f.)
I'll tidy, I'll lay out, I'll arrange
culture: Offering water and Arabic coffee or tea to visitors is basic Gulf hospitality, at the office as at home, so it's part of getting a meeting room ready. Thank the people who did the work with yaʿṭīkum il-ʿāfya; the reply is allāh yʿāfīk.
